lit.summary:
I gathered paged, verbatim readings for the E-PASS design: 19 papers opened as full text through alphaXiv, with PDF pages given and the printed page added where it differs. Nothing was written into docket68, drive/, extracted/, recovered/ or method/. There are two scratch checks (not board evidence): /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Claude-Method-Works/6d820e7d-6d3c-5ac7-8067-527dc14c2847/scratchpad/epass/kr_sympy.py and kr_check.py.

**1. Kaus–Reall (0901.4236): they confirm, by deduction, that SIM2's throat cannot close regularly. They are silent on the depths themselves.**
- **Same equations (computed, sympy, scratch).** Put A = 2mα, R = 2mβ, k = −1 and y = ρ0 − ρ. Then KR's eqs (2.4), (2.6) and (2.7) are exactly SIM2-FACING's p′, q′ and constraint equations; all three differences simplify to 0.
- **Same starting data (READ plus deduced).** With Q = 0, KR's Israel condition (2.16) gives p = q = −1/ℓ, and their (2.17) forces L1 = L2. That is SIM2's start, α = β = 1, AdS2(2m) × S2(2m).
- **No regular member at Q = 0 (READ plus deduced).** KR's regular family closes off where the S² shrinks smoothly (R(0) = 0, R′(0) = 1). Every member of finite size has Q > 0: Q → 0 only as A0 → 0, where ρ0 → 0. So the vacuum-brane throat has no smoothly capped bulk.
- **Same kind of singular end.** KR's singular branch reads "A ... vanishes at some finite value ρ = ρ1. R diverges", a curvature singularity. SIM2 finds α → 0 at y_s^th. The scratch check reproduces y_s^th to four decimals (2.5536, 2.3744, 1.9868, 0.9139, 0.3864) and finds β → ∞ there, with Kasner-like exponents 0.683 and −0.183.
- **One difference.** In KR the singular end lies beyond the brane and is cut away; in SIM2 it lies in the slab that is kept.
- **Silent on the numbers.** KR never integrate from Q = 0 data, so they say nothing about 2.55m (flat) or 0.91m (ℓ = m).
- **Support for S6 (READ).** KR p.4: "if the horizon is degenerate on the brane then it will also be degenerate in the bulk". KLR's Lemma 0 gives the AdS2 warped product in the near-horizon limit. Together these upgrade part of S6 from standard-not-READ.
- **Support for S1 and S6 (READ).** CRSS p.5: a = b on the horizon, which is S6's w_r ≡ 0. CRSS pp.5–6: the trace Riccati equation, which is Lemma T. CRSS show K diverging at finite depth for Weyl-charged data, the extremal tidal-RN case included, but they cannot tell whether that point is singular.

**2. Chamblin–Hawking–Reall and Emparan–Horowitz–Myers.**
- The black string is singular at the AdS horizon, and in RS2 that singularity "will be visible from our domain wall" (CHR p.7). The cigar's horizon "closes off before reaching the AdS horizon" (CHR p.2).
- **Passing RS2's own horizon leads to other walls, not to our plane.** Continuing across RS2's degenerate Poincaré horizon reaches either pure AdS or "infinitely many domain walls" (CHR pp.2–3), or "two Poincare patches" (EHM PDF p.10). That is the between-universes picture; E-PASS is the passage through the object's own horizon.
- **A horizon infinitely far away is still reached.** EHM (PDF p.2): such horizons are "infinitely far from the brane in spacelike directions, but can be reached by observers in finite proper time (just like the horizons of extreme charged black holes)". This is the premise E-PASS needs.
- Large brane black holes are pancakes, extending L_z ≃ ℓ log(2μ) off the brane (EHM).

**3. Figueras–Wiseman and Abdolrahimi et al.** Their static brane black holes are regular because:
- the horizon closes off at an axis where the S² shrinks (with B = C imposed on the horizon), and
- the deep bulk asymptotes to an undisturbed extremal Poincaré horizon,
- with vacuum Israel conditions on the brane.

Their solutions are non-extremal. SIM2's throat bulk has neither a closing axis nor a Poincaré end.

**4. Crossing a degenerate horizon in a bulk with Λ < 0. These are cautions, not refutations.**
- **Horowitz–Kolanowski–Santos (2210.02473).** Generic extremal horizons with Λ < 0 have diverging tidal forces while all scalar invariants stay finite. "Smoothness of the known exact solutions is an artifact of the symmetry". A Taylor expansion from the horizon "clearly assumes smoothness and is generically not allowed". Exponents are integers in 4D with Λ = 0, "but not in higher dimensions".
- **Karasik et al. (gr-qc/0404015).** By Rácz–Wald, the horizon is singular unless its surface gravity is constant. Where it is not, the singularity is "naked from the bulk but ... covered on the brane". A regular horizon needed half-integer powers.
- **What E-PASS must therefore do (deduced; OPEN).** Show κ ≡ 0 at every depth y. Compute the scaling exponents of perturbations about the throat bulk; this bears on the escape E-AN and on item 161. Determine the causal character of the singular end at y_s^th, which bounds the horizon from below.

**5. Throats with two ends, and one universe.**
- **Simpson–Visser at a = 2m is the closest 4D analogue of eq. (17) at r0 = 2m.** It is "a one-way wormhole with an extremal null throat". Its NEC shortfall is negative everywhere except on the horizon, as in SIM2 S5. The far side is a "Copy of our universe". The only one-universe version is a "looped" diagram that identifies the past bounce with the future one; that may run against item 128 ("A genuine loop would me creating a paradox of transition from position 1 to position 1."). This is deduced and OPEN: SV do not discuss closed causal curves.
- **Maldacena–Qi.** Global AdS2's two boundaries are causally connected. A configuration whose dilaton grows toward both ends needs negative integrated null energy: it is "a special case of the general topological censorship result".
- **Galloway–Graf.** No asymptotically AdS2 × S2 spacetime obeys the strict ANEC.
- **Maldacena–Milekhin.** In their RS2 wormhole, topological censorship holds in 5D because the bulk fills in the loop. It needs negative energy, which is classical in 5D, and it has no horizon: a different member from E-PASS.

**6. Topological censorship (GSWW).** The horizon-screening corollary is in hep-th/9912119 (pp.10–11), not in gr-qc/9902061, which supplies its ingredient, Theorem 2.1 (p.8).
- It screens boundary components that are disconnected from each other.
- E-PASS's two ends lie on one connected plane, joined by the plane's own null chain (CURRENT X7). So Theorem 2 does not forbid the passage. The principle of topological censorship asks only that the passage be homotopic to a curve within the plane (deduced).
- Both theorems need a conformal boundary with Ω = 0, which an RS plane does not have (as already filed in OUTSIDE.md).

**7. Other sources.**
- **Pappas–Nakas (2412.19773).** The only published 5D uplift of the CFM / Bronnikov–Kim brane metric. Its bulk carries matter that violates the NEC, unlike clause (B)'s vacuum bulk. It treats only the wormhole branch, not the α = 2M threshold where eq. (17) sits.
- **Bronnikov–Kim.** They hope the bulk will be regular only for horizonless throats, r0 > 2m.
- **Hochberg–Visser.** "Apparent horizons and bifurcation two-spheres ... are not examples of throats" (already filed). Their "semantic games" remark bears on the board's split of P2's stress, H-SPLIT-AT-OUR-TENSION.

**8. Searches.**
- Consensus and SciSpace were searched; their hits led to Pappas–Nakas and Karasik et al.
- Elicit could not be used: the plan has no API access.
- No paper was found on a passage through a bulk horizon between two regions of one brane. The nearest are Maldacena–Milekhin (no horizon, NEC-violating) and the Poincaré-patch continuations in CHR and EHM (to other walls).

**9. Not READ (standard-not-READ):** the Rácz–Wald theorem itself, Carter's extension of extreme Reissner–Nordström, HKS's 5D analysis (deferred to their ref [8]), and the Gregory–Laflamme stability of extremal branes.

(2.16) We can use these to evaluate the Hamiltonian constraint (2.7) at ρ = ρ0, giving k/L1^2 + 1/L2^2 = −ℓ^2Q^4/(2L2^8), (2.17) from which we deduce k = −1, so the metric on the brane is AdS2 × S2, in agreement with 4d GR. However, this equation also implies L1 < L2 ... Note that the geometric interpretation of ρ0 is as the proper length of the horizon in the direction transverse to the brane. [math transcribed]
reads.page: PDF p.6 (eqs 2.16-2.17); Israel condition (2.11) on p.5
reads.bearing: Deduced: with Q = 0 (a matter-free plane, clause (B)), (2.16) gives p = q = −1/l in SIM2's y-orientation, and (2.17) gives −1/L1^2 + 1/L2^2 = 0, i.e. L1 = L2. That is exactly SIM2's start (alpha = beta = 1, p = q = −1/l; eq. (17)'s throat is AdS2(2m) x S2(2m)). For any Q ≠ 0, (2.17) forces L1 < L2 strictly, so equal radii occur only at Q = 0. Caution under 155 (2): KR's rho0 is a horizon length, never M's corridor length (bits).

reads.source: Kaus & Reall, arXiv:0901.4236v1
reads.claim: Regularity requires the horizon to close off in the bulk where the S2 shrinks; R cannot have a local maximum.
reads.quote: In the bulk, compactness of the horizon implies that R(ρ) must vanish somewhere. We can shift ρ so that this occurs at ρ = 0, with R(ρ) > 0 for ρ > 0. Smoothness at ρ = 0 requires that A(ρ) has a Taylor series consisting of even powers of ρ and R(ρ) a Taylor series consisting of odd powers of ρ, with A(0) ≡ A0 > 0, R′(0) = 1. (2.8) ... Note that R is monotonically increasing in the bulk: if it were not then R would have a local maximum, where R′ = 0, and evaluating (2.6) at this point gives R′′ > 0, which is impossible at a local maximum.
reads.bearing: KR's regular solutions end at a smooth tip where R → 0. SIM2's throat bulk never does this. Scratch integration of SIM2's ODEs (kr_check.py, not board evidence): beta has a minimum (1.000 at l = ∞; 0.972 at y = 0.43m for l = 8m; 0.644 at y = 0.63m for l = m) and then grows without bound toward y_s^th, so the bulk horizon over the throat never closes off. KR's no-maximum lemma is the same as SIM2's q' > 0 at q = 0.

reads.source: Kaus & Reall, arXiv:0901.4236v1
reads.claim: Classification of the bulk solutions: a singular branch (A → 0, R → ∞ at a curvature singularity) for A0 < l/2; the Israel condition is met only for 0 < A0 < l, which fixes Q(A0); Q → 0 only as A0 → 0.
reads.quote: For 0 < A0 < ℓ/2, we find that A decreases montonically, and vanishes at some finite value ρ = ρ1. R diverges at ρ = ρ1. A calculation of the square of the Riemann tensor reveals that ρ = ρ1 is a curvature singularity. ... For the AdS5 solution, the Israel equation cannot be satisfied. ... The Israel junction condition can be satisfied if, and only if, 0 < A0 < ℓ, when it determines ρ0 and Q in terms of A0. For 0 < A0 < ℓ/2, we find ρ0 < ρ1, so the curvature singularity at ρ = ρ1 is not present in the spacetime containing the brane. We find that ρ0 and Q are monotonically increasing functions of A0 which vanish as A0 → 0 and diverge as A0 → ℓ.
reads.page: PDF p.7 (to p.8 for the last clause); small-BH scaling L1 ≈ 0.24(lQ^2)^(1/3), L2 ≈ 0.66(lQ^2)^(1/3), rho0 ≈ 0.56(lQ^2)^(1/3) on p.9

By ODE uniqueness, the vacuum-brane data (Q = 0, L1 = L2 = 2m) lie on no regular member, so its bulk cannot cap off smoothly. KR are SILENT on the values y_s^th = 2.5536m (flat) and 0.9139m (l = m); they never integrate from Q = 0 data. The scratch run reproduces SIM2's 2.5536, 2.3744, 1.9868, 0.9139 and 0.3864m.

reads.source: Kaus & Reall, arXiv:0901.4236v1
reads.claim: Surface gravity is constant over the bulk horizon, so a degenerate brane horizon is degenerate throughout the bulk; the near-horizon geometry is a warped product over a 2D constant-curvature space.
reads.quote: Consider a static brane-world black hole. It is natural to assume that the bulk will also be static. In the bulk, the surface gravity is constant. Hence, by continuity, it will take the same value on the brane. Therefore if the horizon is degenerate on the brane then it will also be degenerate in the bulk. We can take a near-horizon limit. It was proven in [16] that the near-horizon geometry of a static extreme black hole can be written in the warped product form
reads.bearing: READ support for SIM2 S6: the bulk horizon over the throat is degenerate at every depth and has AdS2 symmetry. S6 had this as sympy plus standard-not-READ. For E-PASS, the horizon to be crossed is a degenerate Killing horizon at every y in [0, y_s^th).

reads.source: Kaus & Reall, arXiv:0901.4236v1
reads.claim: The bulk near-horizon family does not depend on the brane matter; earlier extremal brane solutions that are not localized are nakedly singular in the bulk.
reads.quote: However, note that our bulk solution is independent of what kind of matter field is present on the brane. Hence the near-horizon geometry of any static, spherically symmetric, extremal black hole solution should have the same solution in the bulk (although possibly with k = 0 or 1). [p.11] ... Exact solutions for which the induced metric on the brane is an extremal black hole were constructed in Ref. [12]. However, the physical significance of these solutions (which involve non-trivial bulk fields other than the metric) is unclear because they are not localized on the brane and are nakedly singular in the bulk, just like the non-extremal solution of Ref. [13]. [footnote 1, p.2]
reads.bearing: KR's family is the right comparator for eq. (17)'s throat, a matter-free plane carrying only Weyl charge: only the junction differs (Q = 0). The footnote is a precedent that extremal brane data without a localizing mechanism give bulk singularities.

reads.source: A. Chamblin, S. W. Hawking and H. S. Reall, 'Brane-world black holes', hep-th/9909205v2 (PRD 61 065007)
reads.claim: The black string is singular at the AdS (Poincare) horizon; the cigar's horizon closes off before reaching it.
reads.quote: We find that the AdS horizon is singular for this black string solution. This is signalled by scalar curvature invariants diverging if one approaches the horizon along the axis of the string. If one approaches the horizon in a different direction then no scalar curvature invariant diverges. However, in a frame parallelly propagated along a timelike geodesic, some curvature components do diverge. ... We will argue that our solution evolves to a "black cigar" solution describing an object that looks like the black string far from the AdS horizon (so the metric on the domain wall is Schwarzschild) but has a horizon that closes off before reaching the AdS horizon. ... We suspect that the AdS horizon will be non-singular for the cigar solution. [OCR ligatures fi/ff restored]
reads.page: PDF p.2; eq. (3.4) R_abcd R^abcd = (1/l^4)(40 + 48M^2 z^4/r^6) 'which diverges at the AdS horizon z = ∞ as well as at the black string singularity at r = 0' on p.4
reads.bearing: The uniform (warped-product) extension of a brane horizon ends singularly; regularity needs a horizon that closes off. SIM2's throat bulk ends at finite depth y_s^th, not at the Poincare horizon, but it shares the black-string defect of no closure, plus KR's singular end.

reads.source: Chamblin, Hawking & Reall, hep-th/9909205v2
reads.claim: In RS2 the AdS-horizon singularity is visible from our wall; CHR regard such singularities as pathological despite the redshift.
reads.quote: This singularity can be removed if we use the first RS model in which there are two domain walls present and we live on a negative tension wall. However if we wish to use the second RS model (with a non-compact fifth dimension) then the singularity will be visible from our domain wall. ... However we regard singularities as a pathology of the theory since, in principle, arbitrarily large fluctuations can emerge from the singularity and the red-shift is finite.
reads.bearing: The same standard the earlier judges applied to sim2_passage: a static singular surface visible from the plane spoils regularity whatever a passage family does. E-PASS must say whether the singular end at y_s^th, and stage 5 F2's off-throat surface, lie in the causal past of any passage (OPEN).

reads.source: Chamblin, Hawking & Reall, hep-th/9909205v2
reads.claim: Continuing across RS2's own bulk horizon: either pure AdS beyond it, or infinitely many further walls.
reads.quote: If one simply slices AdS along a positive tension wall at y = 0 and assumes reflection symmetry then there are several ways to analytically continue the solution across the horizon. These have been discussed in [11,12,13,14]. There are two obvious choices of continuation. The first is simply to assume that beyond the horizon, the solution is pure AdS with no domain walls present. ... An alternative, which seems closer in spirit to the geometry envisaged by RS, is to include further domain walls beyond the horizon, as shown in figure 2. In this case, there are infinitely many domain walls present.
reads.bearing: Deduced: the textbook passage through an RS2 bulk (Poincare) horizon leads away from our plane, to other walls, i.e. a second sheet between universes. E-PASS ('no second sheet; end 2 of our own plane reached through the horizon') goes through the object's own horizon instead, which the literature read does not treat.

reads.source: Chamblin, Hawking & Reall, hep-th/9909205v2
reads.claim: A 5D null geodesic that moves in the extra dimension behaves as a 4D timelike geodesic.
reads.quote: It should not be surprising that a null geodesic in five dimensions is equivalent to a timelike geodesic in four dimensions: the non-trivial motion in the fifth dimension gives rise to a mass in four dimensions.
reads.bearing: For tracing passages: a bulk null passage projects to massive motion on the plane. No identification with M's trajectories (item 118) is implied.

reads.source: R. Emparan, G. T. Horowitz and R. C. Myers, 'Exact description of black holes on branes', hep-th/9911043v2 (JHEP 0001:007)
reads.claim: RS's AdS horizons are degenerate, infinitely far in spacelike directions, yet reached in finite proper time; the exact AdS4 C-metric bulk gives a smooth AdS horizon.
reads.quote: The background solution contains AdS5 horizons which are infinitely far from the brane in spacelike directions, but can be reached by observers in finite proper time (just like the horizons of extreme charged black holes). The linearized modes studied in [1] turn out to be singular on these horizons [5]. [PDF p.2] ... The net result is a solution without conical singularities, with a smooth AdS horizon, and containing a black hole bound to the Planck two-brane. [PDF p.3]
reads.bearing: Precedent for E-PASS's premise: a degenerate horizon that lies infinitely far along a static slice (SIM2 S6) is still crossed in finite proper time. Whether the crossing is smooth depends on the bulk (cf. Horowitz–Kolanowski–Santos).

reads.source: Emparan, Horowitz & Myers, hep-th/9911043v2
reads.claim: In the C-metric the AdS horizon is a degenerate horizon, and the mu = 0 metric continues through it into a second Poincare patch.
reads.quote: There is a second horizon at y = 0 which is degenerate, i.e., has zero Hawking temperature (see Fig. 1), which we will see corresponds to the AdS horizon. [PDF p.8] ... The coordinate transformation (3.5) only holds for y < 0, but the metric (3.1) with μ = 0 holds for all y < x with −1 ≤ x ≤ 1 (with only the usual coordinate singularity associated with the AdS horizon). This covers two Poincare patches, one on each side of the horizon y = 0. [PDF p.10]
reads.bearing: An exact, smooth passage through a degenerate bulk horizon exists in the pure-AdS (mu = 0) case, but it leads to another Poincare patch, not back to the same brane. It is a structural precedent for crossing; it does not realize E-PASS.

reads.source: Emparan, Horowitz & Myers, hep-th/9911043v2
reads.claim: Shape of the brane black hole's horizon in the bulk: a pancake whose proper extent off the brane is about l log(2 mu); the curvature singularity lies on the brane; the AdS horizon is unchanged.
reads.quote: So the black hole is centered on the brane z = ℓ but extends off of it to z_max = ℓ(1 + 2μx2) < ℓ(1 + 2μ) since x2 cannot be greater than one. In contrast, the curvature singularity at y = −∞ is located only on the brane z = ℓ at r = 0. [PDF p.11] ... The black hole extends to z_max = ℓ(1 + 2μx2) ≈ (2μ)^(2/3) ℓ, but this corresponds to a proper distance L_z ≃ ℓ log(2μ). While L_z is much larger than the AdS scale ℓ, it is still much smaller than the extent of the horizon on the brane r = 2μℓ. Hence the large black hole looks like a flattened pancake. [PDF pp.14-15] ... since the AdS horizon is infinitely far away in spatial directions, the field due to sources on the brane is strictly zero at the AdS horizon – the horizon geometry is unchanged. [PDF p.17]
reads.page: PDF p.11 (printed 10), PDF pp.14-15 (printed 13-14), PDF p.17 (printed 16)
reads.bearing: For regular exact brane black holes the bulk horizon is compact and the singularity sits on the brane. SIM2's throat horizon instead runs vertically to a bulk singularity at y_s^th. EHM (PDF p.22) also: 'the Hawking temperature will be the same on the brane and in the bulk spacetime', consistent with KR. Note on phase 3 only: EHM PDF p.18, a negative-tension two-membrane model 'produces negative mass black holes on the brane out of four-dimensional black holes with positive mass'.

reads.source: P. Figueras and T. Wiseman, 'Gravity and large black holes in Randall-Sundrum II braneworlds', arXiv:1105.2558v2 (PRL 107 081101)
reads.claim: Large static RS2 black holes exist; regularity comes from an AdS5-CFT4 bulk that tends to the Poincare horizon in the IR, with vacuum Israel conditions; the horizon is a pancake with a tip; extremal brane black holes are noted as a separate case.
reads.quote: The near horizon geometry of extremal RSII black holes has been determined [25], although extremal solutions are thought to evade the non-existence conjecture. [p.1] ... Provided there exists a static AdS5-CFT4 solution with 4d Schwarzschild as the boundary metric and which asymptotes to the Poincare horizon of AdS in the IR, then large black holes in the RSII scenario exist. [p.2] ... Here we impose the vacuum Israel matching conditions (eq.(3) with the l.h.s. equal to zero) [p.3] ... From these embeddings we see the horizon is pancake-like [32], with a proper distance to the tip going as ∼ ℓ log(R4/ℓ) for large R4/ℓ. ... such a horizon geometry presumably has too little extent into the bulk to experience a Gregory-Laflamme type instability [33]. [p.4]
reads.bearing: What makes FW regular where the black string is not: the horizon has a tip in the bulk, and the deep bulk is the unperturbed Poincare horizon. The solutions are non-extremal (inverse temperature β = 4πβ̃l, p.3). SIM2's throat bulk has neither feature, so FW's mechanism is not available to it. FW's ref [25] is Kaus–Reall.

reads.source: S. Abdolrahimi, C. Cattoen, D. N. Page and S. Yaghoobpour-Tari, 'Large Randall-Sundrum II black holes', arXiv:1206.0708v4 (PLB)
reads.claim: Independent confirmation of FW. The black string is singular at v = 0; the regular solution imposes an axis where the S2 shrinks, a regular black-hole horizon, and an extremal Poincare horizon.
reads.quote: The hypersurfaces of constant v are Schwarzschild metrics of mass m(v) = v/2. The curvature at y > 0 diverges at v = 0, so this black string metric is singular. We modify the metric by adding some y^2 terms to remove this singularity ... The coordinate boundaries are these: x = 0 is the infinite AdS boundary that is conformal to the Schwarzschild metric when we impose A = B = C = D = 1 there, y = 0 is the extremal Poincare horizon, x = 1 is the axis of symmetry where the two-sphere shrinks to zero size and where we impose A = D for regularity, and y = 1 is the black hole horizon where we impose the regularity requirement B = C.
reads.page: p.2 (printed = PDF); p.5: 'the surface gravity of the black hole horizon is exactly 1/(4M), the same as for the Schwarzschild metric' (to first order)
reads.bearing: Same lesson as FW. Regularity = closure at an axis plus the horizon regularity condition B = C, the analogue of CRSS's a = b and SIM2's w_r = 0 on the horizon. E-PASS's bulk should be checked against both: w_r = 0 on the horizon at every depth, and no closure (hence a singular end).

reads.source: A. Chamblin, H. S. Reall, H. Shinkai and T. Shiromizu, 'Charged brane-world black holes', hep-th/0008177v2 (PRD 63 064015)
reads.claim: Gaussian-normal evolution of Weyl-charged (tidal Reissner–Nordström) and Maxwell-charged brane data: a and b evolve synchronously on the horizon; the trace Riccati equation; K diverges at finite chi in all charged cases, the extremal tidal-RN case included.
reads.quote: It was shown in the Appendix of [24] that at the inner boundary r = r+, a and b evolve synchronously, that is, a(T, r+) = b(T, r+). Analytically continuing back to our original spacetime yields the boundary condition a(χ, r+) = b(χ, r+). [p.5] ... K̇ = (4)R − K^2 + 16/ℓ^2 = −K_μν K^μν + 4/ℓ^2 ... k̇ − (2/ℓ)k + (1/4)k^2 = −k̃_μν k̃^μν ≤ 0 [pp.5-6] ... We have therefore proved that if Q ≠ 0 or β ≠ 0 then K diverges before χ = χcrit. ... The horizon will encounter the caustic before reaching the AdS Cauchy horizon. The caustic can therefore be viewed as the endpoint of the horizon, i.e., the tip of the black cigar. Our analysis has only shown that the geodesic slicing must break down at the caustic so, in principle, this point may be regular ... We cannot check whether curvature invariants diverge at χ = χcrit [p.6] ... For all cases (including β > 0), we have found that the trace of the extrinsic curvature diverges at a finite distance from the brane, with the volume element of the spacetime tending to zero. [p.7] [math transcribed]
reads.page: pp.5-7 (printed = PDF); Fig. 1(b) caption p.10: 'Fig.(b) is for the extremal case of model (i), β = M^2'
reads.bearing: (a) A braneworld precedent (READ) for SIM2 S6's w_r ≡ 0 over the horizon (a = b means kappa_t = kappa_r there) and for S1's Lemma T. (b) CONFIRMS a finite-depth breakdown for Weyl-charged data, including a degenerate (extremal) horizon. CRSS cannot say whether the end is regular. SIM2 and KR identify it as a curvature singularity with alpha → 0, a sharper result consistent with CRSS.

reads.source: G. J. Galloway, K. Schleich, D. M. Witt and E. Woolgar, 'Topological censorship and higher genus black holes', gr-qc/9902061v2 (PRD 60 104039)
reads.claim: Theorem 2.1: under global hyperbolicity, a compact cut and a modified ANEC, one boundary-at-infinity component cannot signal another. PTC: boundary-to-boundary causal curves deform to the boundary. The boundary needs Omega = 0.
reads.quote: Theorem 2.1. Let M ⊂ M′ be as described above, and assume the following conditions hold. (i) M′ = M ∪ I is globally hyperbolic. (ii) There is a component I0 of I which admits a compact spacelike cut. (iii) For each point p in M near I0 and any future complete null geodesic s → η(s) in M starting at p, ∫_0^∞ Ric(η′, η′) ds ≥ 0. Then I0 cannot communicate with any other component of I, i.e., J+(I0) ∩ (I∖I0) = ∅. [p.8] ... Assume that D does not meet any other components of ∂M′. Note that if the conditions of Theorem 2.1 hold, this latter assumption is automatically satisfied. [p.8] ... Principle of Topological Censorship (PTC). Every causal curve whose initial and final endpoints belong to I is fixed endpoint homotopic to a curve on I. [p.5] [OCR ligatures restored]
reads.page: p.8 (Thm 2.1); p.5 (PTC); p.7 (conditions (b): Ω = 0 and dΩ ≠ 0 on I)
reads.bearing: Correction of attribution: the horizon-screening corollary is NOT in gr-qc/9902061. It is in the companion hep-th/9912119 (next entry), built on this Theorem 2.1. Deduced: E-PASS's ends 1 and 2 lie on ONE connected plane (joined by the plane's own null chain through the degenerate horizon, CURRENT X7), so Thm 2.1 does not forbid a passage. The PTC would only require the bulk passage to be homotopic to a curve within the plane. Both require Omega = 0, which an RS plane at finite distance lacks; already filed in residue/OUTSIDE.md as not applying as stated.

reads.source: Galloway, Schleich, Witt & Woolgar, 'The AdS/CFT correspondence conjecture and topological censorship', hep-th/9912119v2 (PLB 505 255)
reads.claim: The horizon-screening corollary: a disconnected boundary-at-infinity implies black-hole horizons that screen the components from each other; such spacetimes have both black-hole and white-hole horizons.
reads.quote: An immediate result of theorem 2 is that spacetimes with disconnected I contain black hole horizons which screen the boundary components from each other. Corollary. Let M′ satisfy the conditions given in theorem 1. If I is disconnected, then the spacetime contains black hole horizons, namely J̇−(I0) ≠ ∅. [pp.10-11] ... They both have two disconnected components of I. Causal curves originating from one component of I cannot end on the other; instead they end on the black hole singularity. [p.9] ... In simple terms, these results show that black hole spacetimes formed from the collapse of topological structures must always have both black hole and white hole horizons. [p.11]
reads.bearing: What a horizon does: it screens DISCONNECTED boundary components, which is the between-universes case (phase 3), not E-PASS. Within one universe the plane is one component, so no screening theorem applies. The black-hole and white-hole pair agrees structurally with item 132's 'the passage is one way by nature, a black hole in and a white hole out' (M's words, verbatim). The theorems still need Omega = 0 and ANEC; not applicable as stated to an RS plane.

reads.source: H. K. Kunduri, J. Lucietti and H. S. Reall, 'Near-horizon symmetries of extremal black holes', arXiv:0705.4214v3
reads.claim: Lemma 0: a static near-horizon geometry is locally a warped product of a 2D maximally symmetric spacetime (AdS2 for black holes) with the horizon cross-section; global if the horizon is simply connected.
reads.quote: Lemma 0. A static near-horizon geometry is locally a warped product of a 2d maximally symmetric space-time with a compact (D − 2)-manifold. [p.4] ... The word "locally" can be deleted if the horizon is simply connected. For a static black hole V must be timelike outside the horizon. After taking the near-horizon limit, this gives F0 ≤ 0 so the de Sitter case is excluded. So in general, the near-horizon geometry of a static extremal black hole is locally a warped product of AdS2 or R1,1 with a compact (D − 2)-manifold. [p.5]
reads.bearing: READ basis for SIM2 S6's homogeneity over the throat in the near-horizon limit (AdS2 warped over y and S2), which S6 carried as 'uniqueness in the analytic class (standard, not READ)'. Caveat (deduced): the Lemma is stated for a compact (D−2)-manifold, but SIM2's bulk horizon cross-section S2 x [0, y_s^th) ends at a singularity. The local statement is what transfers.

reads.source: G. T. Horowitz, M. Kolanowski and J. E. Santos, 'Almost all extremal black holes in AdS are singular', arXiv:2210.02473v3
reads.claim: With Lambda < 0, generic extremal horizons have diverging tidal forces (null singularity, finite scalar invariants). Smoothness of known solutions is an artifact of symmetry. Taylor expansions from the horizon are fine-tuned. Exponents are integers only in 4D with Lambda = 0.
reads.quote: When the cosmological constant is negative, we show that (in almost all cases) tidal forces diverge as one crosses the horizon, and this singularity is stronger for larger black holes. ... Nevertheless, all scalar curvature invariants remain finite. [abstract, PDF p.1] ... The symmetry of AdS2 ensures that all perturbations should have power law behavior near an extremal horizon. If the exponent is not an integer, the solution is not C∞, and if the exponent is too small, the curvature will diverge. [PDF p.3] ... Smoothness of the known exact solutions is an artifact of the symmetry rather than a basic physical feature. ... However when Λ = 0, one finds that all exponents are positive integers and so the metric is indeed smooth. ... They turn out to be integers in four dimensions, but not in higher dimensions. ... Unfortunately, the starting point of that analysis was the Taylor expansion in the distance from the horizon. This clearly assumes smoothness and is generically not allowed. Thus, one should rather see these results (at least with Λ ≠ 0) as a search for very special, fine-tuned solutions. [PDF p.4]
reads.page: PDF pp.1, 3-4 (printed 2-3); footnote 4 at PDF p.9 (printed 8): 'If γ > 1/2 ... one can extend the fields inside the horizon as a weak solution, but the extension is not unique'; PDF p.35 (printed 34): 'The event horizon is a Cauchy horizon for any complete spacelike surface outside the black hole.'
reads.bearing: The main caution for E-PASS (deduced; OPEN). E-PASS crosses a degenerate horizon in a Lambda5 < 0 bulk. The crossing is smooth only if every perturbation of the AdS2-symmetric throat bulk scales with integer powers in the regular coordinate (u, with r = 2m + u^2). That includes the y-dependent modes that carry the solution off the near-horizon profile toward the owner's bulk. The board's analytic series (b4_static; SIM2's O(x) expansion; S7's sqrt(x) profiles) is the kind of 'Taylor expansion' HKS call fine-tuned; this bears on escape E-AN and item 161. HKS treat 4D Einstein–Maxwell; their 5D statement is deferred to their ref [8] (standard-not-READ). Not a refutation: the board's configuration keeps spherical symmetry, and the relevant exponents must be computed.

reads.source: D. Karasik, C. Sahabandu, P. Suranyi and L. C. R. Wijewardhana, 'Small black holes on branes: is the horizon regular or singular?', gr-qc/0404015v2 (PRD 70 064007)
reads.claim: By Racz–Wald, a horizon whose surface gravity varies along it is singular. The integer-power construction gives such a horizon, naked from the bulk but covered on the brane; regularity needs half-integer powers.
reads.quote: According to a theorem by Rácz and Wald [16], if the surface gravity is not constant on the horizon, the horizon is singular. [p.3] ... So, according to Eq.(11), although the horizon is singular, the singularity is naked from the bulk but it is covered on the brane. [p.6] ... In first order of ǫ we show that the iteration of the weak field solution, which includes only integer powers of the mass, leads to a solution that has a singular horizon. We find a solution with a regular horizon but its asymptotic expansion in the mass also contains half integer powers. [abstract, p.1]
reads.bearing: Deduced: E-PASS's bulk horizon must have kappa constant (here zero) at every depth y. On SIM2's throat metric alpha(y)^2[−(x/2)dt^2 + dx^2/x^2], kappa → 0 at every y, which is consistent. Once the bulk is continued off the throat (the owner's series) across x = 0, constancy must be verified, or the crossing meets a singularity 'naked from the bulk but ... covered on the brane'. Like HKS, a regular horizon may require non-integer powers (E-AN). The setting is RS1, small mass. The Racz–Wald theorem itself is standard-not-READ.

reads.source: A. Simpson and M. Visser, 'Black-bounce to traversable wormhole', arXiv:1812.07114v3 (JCAP 02 (2019) 042)
reads.claim: At a = 2m the metric is a one-way wormhole whose null throat is an extremal horizon. Its NEC shortfall is negative everywhere except on the horizon. Maximally extended, the far side is a copy of our universe; a looped version identifies past and future bounces.
reads.quote: If a = 2m, then as r → 0 from either above or below, we have dr/dt → 0. Hence we have a horizon at coordinate location r = 0. However, this geometry is not a black hole. Rather, it is a one-way wormhole with an extremal null throat at r = 0. [PDF p.4] ... Similarly for the null case a = 2m the null throat is located at the horizon r = 0. Note that in this instance the wormhole geometry is only one-way traversable. ... As an alternative construction we can identify the past null bounce at r = 0 with the future null bounce at r = 0 yielding the 'looped' Carter–Penrose diagram of figure 3. [PDF p.5] ... ρ + p‖ = −a^2 |√(r^2 + a^2) − 2m| / (4πG_N (r^2 + a^2)^(5/2)), (5.5) which now holds for all values of r and is negative everywhere except on any horizon that may potentially be present. [PDF p.12] ... For a = 2m the null horizon (one-way throat) is seen to be extremal. [PDF p.13]
reads.page: PDF pp.4-6 (printed 3-5; Fig. 2 'Our Universe' / 'Copy of our universe'; Fig. 3 'Identify time coordinate'), PDF pp.12-13 (printed 11-12)
reads.bearing: The closest 4D GR analogue of eq. (17) at r0 = 2m (deduced): the area radius has its minimum on a degenerate horizon, and the NEC shortfall vanishes only there (cf. SIM2 S5, which reads it as the appearance of item 117 / 120). The passage end 1 → end 2 is one way (item 132; item 143 A 'the only thing that can cross is that which can cross the horizon of a black hole.'). 'Within one universe' is a global choice. The maximal extension gives a COPY of our universe; SV's only one-universe version identifies the past bounce with the future bounce in time. Deduced and OPEN: such an identification may produce closed causal curves, which would run against item 128 ('A genuine loop would me creating a paradox of transition from position 1 to position 1.', M's words, typing kept). SV do not discuss causal loops.

reads.source: J. Maldacena and X.-L. Qi, 'Eternal traversable wormhole', arXiv:1804.00491v3
reads.claim: Global AdS2's two boundaries are causally connected. With a dilaton growing toward both boundaries, a static traversable configuration needs matter that violates the integrated NEC (a case of topological censorship); in the thermal (horizon) configuration no signal crosses.
reads.quote: AdS2 is a very simple two dimensional spacetime that has two asymptotic boundaries. Furthermore, AdS2, viewed as a global spacetime, has two boundaries that are causally connected. We can send a signal from one boundary to the other. It behaves like a traversable wormhole! [PDF p.3] ... For this solution, the two boundary trajectories correspond to lines of constant ρ in the Rindler/Thermal coordinates (2.2), and we cannot send signals between the boundaries. ... There is no solution of this kind in the pure JT gravity with no matter (2.5). Furthermore, there is no solution of this kind if we assume that we have matter which obeys the integrated null energy condition in the bulk. ... This problem is a special case of the general topological censorship result [24, 25] that forbids traversable wormholes and non-trivial topology [PDF p.7]
reads.bearing: Deduced: eq. (17)'s throat is AdS2 x S2 with the S2 radius growing toward BOTH ends (r = 2m + u^2), the analogue of MQ's dilaton growing toward both boundaries. A two-way static passage would need negative integrated null energy. The plane supplies its own apparent shortfall (the Weyl term), which the board reads as the 'appearance' (items 117 / 120; Lemma J of the earlier design). What eq. (17) offers is the one-way crossing of a degenerate horizon, not a horizonless global-AdS2 link.

reads.source: G. J. Galloway and M. Graf, 'Rigidity of asymptotically AdS2 x S2 spacetimes', arXiv:1803.10529v2
reads.claim: Asymptotically AdS2 x S2 spacetimes obeying the NEC are rigid: null lines join the two ends, and no such spacetime obeys the strict ANEC; with parallel Ricci they are isometric to AdS2 x S2.
reads.quote: One of the main results leading to the proof of Theorem 1.1, Proposition 3.3, together with a known result concerning the existence of null conjugate points [14, 2] confirms that there do not exist any asymptotically AdS2 ×S2 spacetimes obeying the strict ANEC. [p.2] ... Theorem 1.2. Let (M, g) be an asymptotically AdS2 × S2 spacetime that satisfies the NEC. If the Ricci tensor is covariant constant then (M, g) is globally isometric to AdS2 × S2. [p.3] ... Proposition 3.3. For any u ∈ R there exists a complete null line ηu : (−∞, ∞) → M with past end eventually contained in M1 and future end eventually contained in M2 [p.11]
reads.bearing: Two-ended AdS2 x S2 throats whose ends are joined by null lines sit exactly on the NEC's edge: rigid and totally geodesic (4D). Deduced: an end-to-end passage through such a throat cannot also carry strictly positive null energy. This is consistent with SIM2's finding that the shortfall vanishes only on the throat. It is a 4D theorem with AdS2 x S2 asymptotics, not the board's 5D bulk.

reads.source: J. Maldacena and A. Milekhin, 'Humanly traversable wormholes', arXiv:2008.06618v2
reads.claim: A wormhole with both mouths on one RS2 brane and an AdS2 x S2 throat: topological censorship should work in 5D because the 5D geometry fills in the loop; traversability needs negative energy, which is classical in 5D; the throat has no horizon.
reads.quote: The topological censorship theorems say that in classical general relativity we cannot have a non-trivial first homotopy group, π1. This is allowed when quantum effects are included. However, what looks like a quantum Casimir energy in four dimensions is actually a classical effect in five dimensions (the negative classical energy of AdS3). So in five dimensions the topological censorship should work. It indeed works because the classical geometry in five dimensions has a trivial π1. More physically, in four dimensions, the null ray that goes through the wormhole cannot be deformed continuously into one that stays outside the wormhole. This is possible by moving the light ray into the fifth dimension. [PDF p.12] ... In classical general relativity, they are forbidden by the average null energy condition [1, 2, 3]. Interestingly, they are allowed in the quantum theory, but with one catch, the time it takes to go through the wormhole should be longer than the time it takes to travel between the two mouths on the outside [PDF p.2] ... AdS2 is boost invariant, so the traveller does not feel anything special. However, we also need to take into account that there could be small non-boost invariant perturbations to the metric [PDF p.14]
reads.bearing: The nearest literature to 'two positions of one plane joined through the bulk within one universe'. It differs from E-PASS: horizonless, held open by negative energy (classical AdS3 in 5D), with the mouths far apart. Deduced: in 5D a passage between two regions of one brane is compatible with topological censorship when the bulk makes it homotopic to a path in the brane. The boost-invariance remark gives tidal safety across an exact AdS2 throat, with the same caveat as HKS about non-boost-invariant perturbations. The traversal-time remark is not to be turned into a distance or speed claim (items 101 (7), 139 (4)).

reads.source: K. A. Bronnikov and S.-W. Kim, 'Possible wormholes in a brane world', gr-qc/0212112v1
reads.claim: Eq. (17) is a symmetric wormhole for r0 > 2m; its NEC combination; the r0 = 2m edge is not discussed for eq. (17). The authors hope horizonless wormholes have regular bulks.
reads.quote: This is evidently a symmetric wormhole geometry for any r0 > 2m ≥ 0, or for any r0 > 0 in case m < 0. ... ρ + p_rad = −(r − 2m)(r0 − 3m/2)/(r^2 (r − 3m/2)^2). (18) [p.4] ... Evidently, r0 = 2m leads to the extreme Reissner-Nordström black hole metric [p.4, Example 3] ... The other is the global regularity of wormhole space-times, and one can expect that the bulk incorporating them will also be regular. [p.6] [math transcribed]
reads.bearing: Deduced: at r0 = 2m, eq. (18) vanishes at the throat r = 2m and is negative for r > 2m (SIM2 S5). BK are SILENT on eq. (17) at r0 = 2m; their analogue for extreme RN says r0 = 2m 'leads to the extreme Reissner-Nordström black hole metric'. Their hope of a regular bulk concerns horizonless throats (r0 > 2m), not the degenerate-horizon throat that clause (G) fixes.

reads.source: T. D. Pappas and T. Nakas, 'On the uplift of 4D wormholes in braneworld models and their 5D structure', arXiv:2412.19773v2 (JHEP 2025)
reads.claim: The only published 5D uplift (GEA) of the CFM / Bronnikov–Kim brane metrics. The CFM family has a WH/BH threshold at alpha/(2M) = 1. In RS-II the uplift needs bulk stress that violates the NEC on the hyperthroat, and the throat shrinks into the bulk.
reads.quote: α/(2M) ∈ (1, +∞) : Isometric traversable WH. Here α is identified with the radius of the wormhole throat. • α/(2M) = 1 : WH/BH threshold. [PDF p.18] ... (ρE + pρ)/k^2 = 3(1 − 2M/α)(3M/α − 2)^(−1) (1 + (kα)|cos χ|)/(kα)^2 < 0 , (4.9) which is always negative for RS-II braneworld CFM wormholes, since α/(2M) > 1 and kα > 0. Consequently, the above analysis showcases that a theory of the form (3.56) will always lead to the violation of null energy conditions. [PDF p.21] ... Hence, the wormhole throat is shrinking as we move away from the brane. [PDF p.21] ... their herein presented 5D bulk uplift provides for the first time in the literature an answer to the question regarding their higher-dimensional structure in the bulk. [PDF p.32]
reads.bearing: Deduced: eq. (17) at r0 = 2m is CFM's 'WH/BH threshold' (alpha = r0), which PN do not treat (wormhole branch only). Their bulk is not vacuum: it carries matter that violates the NEC, unlike clause (B)'s vacuum Lambda5 bulk. So no literature supplies a vacuum bulk for E-PASS's plane; the board's own bulk (b4_static, the SIM2 throat ODE) remains the only one, consistent with the earlier Maartens–Koyama filing.

reads.source: D. Hochberg and M. Visser, 'The null energy condition in dynamic wormholes', gr-qc/9802048v3 (PRL 81 746)
reads.claim: Horizons are excluded from the throat theorem. Splitting the stress into exotic and normal parts is a 'semantic game'; the total stress decides. A wormhole can be one-way or two-way traversable.
reads.quote: Apparent horizons and bifurcation two-spheres fail to satisfy these strict inequalities and so are not examples of throats. [p.3] ... One way of playing semantic games is to arbitrarily divide the total stress energy into an "exotic component" plus a "normal component". As seen above, the total stress energy must always violate the NEC, but it is sometimes possible to force all the NEC violations into the "exotic component" of the stress-energy and keep the "normal component" well-behaved. [p.3] ... the relative motion of the two throats can be such as to render the wormhole either one-way traversable or two-way traversable [p.2]
reads.bearing: Confirms M-PDF-ASTRO filing (iv) verbatim: a degenerate-horizon throat is outside HV's theorem, so E-PASS through it is not forced to violate the NEC at the throat. Deduced: HV's 'semantic games' remark bears on the board's splits of position 2's stress (H-SPLIT-AT-OUR-TENSION vs H-LAW-READ-BY-TRACE) and on reading the Weyl term as an appearance. HV judge by the total stress, which in 5D is the bulk's vacuum (NEC exact).

reads.source: V. E. Hubeny, D. Marolf and M. Rangamani, 'Black funnels and droplets from the AdS C-metrics', arXiv:0909.0005v2
reads.claim: In exact AdS4 C-metrics, degenerate bulk horizons occur and can be smooth (horizons merging into a smooth extreme horizon; a degenerate root as the bulk Poincare horizon). Droplet horizons close off (compact); funnel horizons extend into the bulk.
reads.quote: For λ = 0 we encounter a double root at the origin, which is degenerate and corresponds to the bulk Poincaré horizon. [PDF p.12] ... The y1 and y2 horizons merge to form a smooth extreme horizon when λ = 0. [PDF p.15] ... In contrast, black funnel horizons were non-compact, and extended into the bulk region associated with the boundary γμν asymptopia [PDF p.10]
reads.bearing: Smooth degenerate bulk horizons exist in exact, highly symmetric solutions, consistent with HKS's 'artifact of the symmetry'. Deduced classification: SIM2's throat horizon is neither droplet-like (compact) nor funnel-like (reaching an asymptotic region); it ends on a singular surface at y_s^th. That is the structural difference E-PASS must face. The setting has no RS brane (boundary metric only).

designs.physical_setup:
**Units and scan.** m = 1 (exact scaling, not an illustrative member). The ℓ scanned are the nine of SIM2: ∞, 32, 16, 8, 4, 2, 1, ½, ¼. ℓ is scanned, not hypothesised (140; 136 (8)). Our plane carries eq. (17) (clause (G)) at our tension (s = 1). The bulk is vacuum with Λ₅ = −6/ℓ², static (141, H-QUASI-STATIC-CORRIDOR), one-sided and Z₂-mirrored.

**1. The horizon-penetrating throat bulk (built; sympy).**
- Throat bulk through O(x) (SIM2 S7): ds² = dy² + α²[−(x/2)(1 + x a₁)dt² + (dx²/x²)(1 + x b₁)] + 4β²(1 + x c₁)dΩ².
- Carried to the ingoing Eddington–Finkelstein chart by x = u² and v = t + T(u), with T′ = √2 r√(2r − 3)/u² (the plane's exact tortoise, independent of y). At zeroth order this gives ds² = dy² + α²[−(u²/2)dv² + 2√2 dv du] + 4β²dΩ².
- Checks (computed): g_vu(0) and g_uu(0) as in the ground stage; κ² = u²(4α′² + 1)/8, so the horizon is vertical and degenerate at every depth.
- One way, 1 → 2 (deduced). This matches plane.py P1 and 132.
- **The plane's own chain is acknowledged (CURRENT X7).** Ends 1 and 2 are already joined along the plane through the degenerate horizon. E-PASS does not ask whether they are joined. It asks whether that joining, and the README's continuation into end 2, has a regular causal past.

**2. Three bulk families under the same throat (eq. (17)'s induced AdS₂(2m) × S²(2m), α = β = 1 at y = 0).**
- **(a) Pure tension:** p = q = −1/ℓ. This is SIM2 / Kaus–Reall at Q = 0.
- **(b) The conic of all SL(2) × SO(3)-invariant Israel data:** p² + q² + 4pq = 6/ℓ², i.e. 3s² − t² = 12/ℓ² with s = p + q and t = p − q.
  - On our plane the stress is S^a_b = −ν(K^a_b − δK).
  - Radial NEC: ρ + p_r ≡ 0 (AdS₂ boost invariance).
  - Angular NEC: ρ + P = νt.
  - Tension-subtracted energy: ρ_m = −ν[(3s − t)/2 + 3/ℓ].
  - Trace reading: s_τ = −ℓs/2.
  - On H-LAW-READ-BY-TRACE (our law by trace, s = −2/ℓ) the conic forces t = 0 (deduced). Only on H-SPLIT-AT-OUR-TENSION is there room for README stress.
- **(c) Position 2's sheet P2 at depth y = d + f(u)** (S7/S15 classes), with the slab between the two sheets:
  - power law f = c·u^{2λ};
  - smooth f = g₁u + g₂u², with g₁ > 0: the approach class, including coinciding as d → 0;
  - band g₁ = 0, g₂ > 0, d ∈ [y*, y_s).

**3. The first correction off the throat (the O(x) system).**
- These are SIM2's a₁, b₁, c₁ equations (sim2_facing.throat_rhs). Also re-derived for general order x^λ in sympy; that system reproduces the coded one exactly at λ = 1.
- Plane data: a₁ = −½, b₁ = 5/2, c₁ = 1 (eq. (17), fixed).
- The three y-derivatives at the plane are the O(x) part of the plane's stress. The momentum constraint, −¾a₁′ + ¼b₁′ − c₁′ + c₁(p − q) = 0, and the O(x) Hamiltonian constraint leave one free number μ.
- On a background that closes, regularity at the axis (β → 0) is imposed by a Frobenius analysis at the regular singular point. The axis-shift gauge mode c₁ ~ 2δ/(y_c − y) is allowed. The mode with a₁ ~ 1/(y_c − y) and a logarithm in c₁ is not.
- Plane matter at O(x):
  - radial null part (ρ + p_r) = ν x(a₁′ − b₁′)/2;
  - in the E-normalised crossing direction at the horizon, T_kk = ν(a₁′ − b₁′), finite at u = 0.
  - The SMS split (READ via bulk/signdim.py: SMS eqs. 1, 2, 8–10) is R_kk = κ₄²τ_kk + κ₅⁴π_kk − E_kk. Here κ₄²ν = 2/ℓ, κ₅⁴ = 4/ν², and π_kk = T_kk(ρ_m/3 + P_m/6) (deduced from SMS's π on AdS₂-invariant leading stress).

**4. Causal machinery (from the ground stage, recomputed in the instrument).**
- **Conformal frame:** dη² + ĝ_AdS₂ with η = ∫dy/α. The AdS₂ criterion for J⁻(P_c) at the crossing P_c = (y = 0, u = 0, v_c).
- **Past-directed null geodesics** checked against the conformal prediction.
- **Budgets:** the dynamic-programme budget g(η), in advanced time, with the path held in the throat (x ≤ x_lim). The owner's columns use b4d_stage5 and sim2_bank.json's Padé singular depths 'ys' (the reach census).
- **Global-AdS₂ optical sphere (deduced):** (L²/sin²σ)(−dτ² + dσ²) + dη² is conformal to −dτ² + [dσ² + sin²σ d(η/L)²], so the least global time from a layer at conformal depth η_s to the throat centre is the great-circle distance on the unit S²: min(η_s/L, π/2). A boundary-to-boundary crossing takes π.

**5. Classification of what can sit in a past (each a curvature singularity or a breakdown):**
- an end at finite conformal depth (Kasner, η_s < ∞);
- sheet stress unbounded in EF (freely falling) components;
- a pinch, where the slab's thickness → 0 on the passage (a non-manifold double wedge);
- an unbalanced crease.

A conformal boundary that takes data is a cost, not a breakdown (174 (1); stage 5 F6).

**Guards.** Depths (y_c, d, y*, y_s) are locations, never the corridor's length (155 (2)). Budgets are hold lengths for the cone premise. Nothing is a transit time, distance or speed (139 (4)); the address guard is imported.
designs.the_question_it_decides:
**The decision.** Within one universe, at our tension, with eq. (17) on our plane: does any configuration your rulings admit carry the README across the corridor object's own horizon, and on into end 2, with no curvature singularity in the causal past of the crossing or of its continuation? This is 174 (1)'s strict rule, through an advanced-time hold of at least W = 2.0×10⁵ clocks (o3_write W3, kept by 163). It is decided near the throat, inside the O(x) domain. It is decided separately for E-PASS proper (no second sheet), for position 2's sheet (172, 174), and for the coupled ends (177).

**DQ1. E-PASS proper (no second sheet).**
- The instrument proves or refutes, by computation, that the regular near-horizon bulks over eq. (17)'s throat on a positive-tension plane are exactly one per ℓ: the smooth cap.
  - It then computes the cap's README stress at the throat (NEC and sign of energy).
  - It solves the cap's first correction off the throat with axis regularity.
- The decisive number is c_r(ℓ), the radial null part of our plane's O(x) stress that keeps the cap regular.
- **Outcome A: c_r ≥ 0 at some ℓ.**
  - E-PASS is regular near the throat with NEC-obeying, positive README stress at the throat, on H-README-AT-THE-THROAT.
  - B4d's E-PASS row moves to "regular near the throat; the global static problem (E-DIR: eq. (17) as Dirichlet data plus README stress, regular bulk) open".
  - O3 moves with B4d: near the throat the hold's cone no longer reaches a singularity.
- **Outcome B: c_r < 0 at every ℓ (the scratch pilot's finding at eight of the nine).**
  - E-PASS without a second sheet is refuted under H-NEC-NEVER-VIOLATED (117/120 read strictly; P-NEC-BRANE).
  - The conjunction is small: (G) eq. (17); our tension (H-SPLIT-AT-OUR-TENSION); vacuum Λ₅; static; Z₂ one-sided; KR's near-horizon premise (p.4 READ; their ref. [16] not READ); analytic in u; O(x).
